takeaways: 101.5 bn barrels (6.5% of the world) at one of the lowest costs per barrel
About 40% of the gas Kuwait uses is imported LNG, mostly from Qatar
Al-Zour lifted refining to 1.4 mb/d; in 2024 product exports beat crude
93% of crude goes to Asia, and every export cargo must pass Hormuz
next: KPC targets 4 million b/d of capacity by 2035, plus offshore discoveries and more non-associated gas.
notes_takeaways: To conclude: Kuwait has one of the world's largest and cheapest oil resource bases, but it depends on oil for more than 90% of its exports and income. Its gas is mostly associated with oil, so it now imports about 40% of its gas as LNG. The Al-Zour refinery and the Clean Fuels Project have turned Kuwait into a large exporter of refined products. Its customers are overwhelmingly Asian, and the 2026 Hormuz disruption showed how exposed a Gulf-only export route is. Looking ahead, KPC's strategy targets 4 million b/d of production capacity by 2035, development of the new offshore discoveries, and more non-associated Jurassic gas.
